title: Storing trait objects in collections
prompt: Why can you not store `Vec<dyn Trait>` directly, and how does `Box` solve this?
answer: Every type implementing a trait can have a different size in memory, but vector elements must all have the same known size at compile time. Placing the trait object inside `Box<dyn Trait>` converts it into a fat pointer with a fixed size. The vector stores these pointer handles on the stack while the data lives on the heap.
